newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cement maker CBR sees more after 1996 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Cement maker CBR sees more after 1996 profit rise.

text.p: Leading Belgian cement maker CBR, a unit of Germany's Heidelberger Zement, on Wednesday reported a strong rise in group net profits for 1996 and the prospects of more to come.
Group net profit rose 12.1 percent from 1995 to 4.335 billion francs on a turnover up 13.2 percent to 56.352 billion francs.
The company said it would pay a dividend of 95 francs per share, a rise of 9.2 percent from 1995 taking account of the five-for-one share split in May 1996.
Earnings per share, also taking into account the share split, rose to 192 francs from 171. Analysts had expected a figure of around 200 francs.

Operating income rose 7.0 percent to 7.345 billion francs thanks to a combination of a significant improvement in earnings in North America -- particularly California -- and the start of contributions from its new Turkish operations.
"Californina enjoyed a significant upturn in activity following the first signs of recovery in 1995 which had been held back by bad weather conditions," it said in a statement.
CBR said the rise in group net profit was mainly due to the increase to 100 percent in the shareholdings by itself and Heidelberger in Dutch firm ENCI NV.

The firm said operating income fell slightly in Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany's North Rhine-Westphalia province, with sales of cement and ready-mix concrete being hit by the hard winter and strong competition.
It also reported declining operating income in Central Europe due to tough competition in the Polish market.
CBR bought 60 percent of Polish aggregates company Zielonogorskie Kopalnie Surowcow Mineralnych (ZKSM) in September through its Gorazde unit.
In 1995 ZKSM sold 2.7 million tonnes of aggregates for 33.3 million zlotys, or around 315 million Belgian francs.
Early last year CBR took a 97.7 percent stake in Turkey's Canakkale Cimento -- immediately adding 20 percent to the total cement capacity of the group.

Half of the stake was swapped a few months later for a 30 percent stake in Turkey's Akcimento. As of October 1, the merged entity was renamed Akcansa, 79.4 percent owned in equal parts by the CBR and Sabanci groups.
Akcansa has annual cement production capacity of 5.4 million tonnes, of which 30 percent is exported.
CBR said operating income in Turkey was in line with its expectations.
"Prospects in North America and Central Europe are good, while Western European markets should register a slight rise only," the company said of the outlook for 1997.

"Turkey should gradually increase its contribution to the Group's net income. The expansion of the activities in China will be pursued. Other market openings throughout the world will continue to be sought," it added.

Analysts said on Monday they expected CBR shares, which with a year-to-date rise of just under 20 percent have mildly outperformed the Brussels Bel-20's .BFX 17 percent rise and the construction sector's near 17 percent rise, to get a new lease of life from the results.
The shares ended Wednesday up 40 francs at 3,500 francs before the results were announced.
